Why the Quran is from God

He read no book before it

The Quran says its reciter had recited no scripture and written none before it came.

The Quran tells its own Prophet, before his people, that he recited no book before this and wrote none with his hand. Otherwise, it adds, doubters would have had their case. The claim is narrow, and that is its strength. It was spoken among neighbours who had known him all his life and were eager to answer him. The book rests its case where they could check it.

﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُوا۟ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِن كِتَـٰبٍ وَلَا تَخُطُّهُۥ بِيَمِينِكَ ۖ إِذًا لَّٱرْتَابَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. Then [i.e., otherwise] the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:48

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَرَحْمَةً وَذِكْرَىٰ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And is it not sufficient for them that We revealed to you the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] which is recited to them? Indeed in that is a mercy and reminder for a people who believe.

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:51

You might ask

QuestionCould he have learned by ear?
AnswerPeople in his day said so, and the Quran answers that the source is God. Verse 29:48 speaks of books, not of hearing. What he may have heard remains a fair question.Quran · Al-Furqan 25:5-6
QuestionDid he never write, in his whole life?
AnswerThe verse speaks only of the time before the Quran. Reports differ about later years, and scholars leave that open. The claim stays narrow on purpose.Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:48
QuestionDoes this show he could not have known?
AnswerNo. Arabia had Jews and Christians, and stories travelled. It shows where the book places its case: no scripture behind him, and everything credited to what reached him.Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:51

The claim is small enough to check, and it was made where people could.
